About.metaDescription: How Bloomprint turns yard inspiration into a buildable plan — and the principles behind it.
About.title: About Bloomprint
About.intro: Bloomprint turns yard inspiration into a buildable plan — what to buy, how much, what tools, in what order, and what can go wrong.
About.how1: 1. Tell us your goal, region, budget, and how much work you want to do.
About.how2: 2. A deterministic engine picks and scores plants, then builds the shopping list, budget, install timeline, and risks.
About.how3: 3. You refine with one tap (cheaper, easier, more privacy…), save, compare versions, and share.
About.diff1Bold: The plan is the source of truth, not the AI.
About.diff1: A rules-based engine builds every plan and works fully with no AI key. AI only rephrases and illustrates — it never invents plants, prices, or facts.
About.diff2: Prices are ranges, not quotes. Regions and zones are shown as “likely / approximate.” Assumptions are surfaced, never hidden.
About.diff3: Grouped “Buy First / Can Wait / Optional” shopping, a print-ready store list, weekend install timeline, and calendar care reminders.
About.privacyBody: Your account, profile, and saved plans are stored on your device. Share links encode a plan's inputs, not your data. Photos you add stay in your browser and are never saved. Analytics is cookieless and counts actions, not people.

Guide.title: How to turn a yard idea into a buildable weekend plan.
Guide.intro: A practical checklist for reading a Bloomprint plan, making safe pivots, and avoiding the common mistakes that make suburban yard projects expensive.
Guide.step1Body: Privacy, curb appeal, shade, low upkeep, or pollinators. Bloomprint translates that into plant roles and a build order.
Guide.step2Body: Unknown sun, soil, drainage, and local stock lower confidence. Use the accuracy prompts before buying.
Guide.step3Body: Buy First gets the project buildable. Can Wait and Optional upgrades are where you pivot if budget or hauling gets tight.
Guide.step4Body: Mark the bed, prep soil, place everything first, then plant tall-to-short and finish with edging or mulch.
Guide.storeRule1: Call before driving for plants, heavy materials, or large quantities.
Guide.storeRule2: Substitute by role, mature size, sun tolerance, and maintenance before flower color.
Guide.storeRule3: Do not tighten plant spacing just to make a first-day bed look full.
Guide.storeRule4: Use delivery or mulch pivots when stone, soil, or truck access becomes the blocker.
Guide.notPretend1: It does not know exact store inventory, aisle location, or live prices.
Guide.notPretend2: It does not replace local plant tags, bylaws, utility locates, or professional site work.
Guide.notPretend3: It treats AI as wording help only, never as the source of plant or safety facts.
Guide.notPretend4: It keeps working with no photo, no account, no API key, and no paid data source.

Evidence.openDataNote: No paid keys. Plant names and invasive context come from GBIF, hardiness from USDA, and the planting window from regional climatology — all free and cached, so the app never blocks on an API.

Toolbox.title: Landscape Toolbox
Toolbox.intro: Quick, honest landscaping math — works offline, no AI needed. Every result is a range with its assumptions shown.

common.disclaimer: Estimate only. Measure your space and confirm quantities before buying.
common.emptyBody: Fill in the fields to see your estimate.

Copilot.title: Ask about {section}

promptsTimeline: Can I do it in one weekend?

mulch.title: Mulch Calculator
mulch.intro: How many bags of mulch you need for a bed, at a safe depth.
mulch.depthWarningBody: More than 3 in can suffocate roots and rot stems. Keep mulch 2–3 in deep, and pull it back from trunks and crowns.
mulch.assumeBag: One bag = {size} cu ft of mulch.
mulch.assumeDepth: Depth: {depth} in across the whole bed.
mulch.assumeBuffer: Includes a {pct}% buffer for settling and uneven coverage.
mulch.emptyBody: Fill in the dimensions and depth to see how much mulch to buy.
mulch.formula: bags = ⌈ area × depth ÷ bag volume ⌉ + buffer
mulch.how: Area × depth is how much mulch fills the bed. We round up to whole bags and add a buffer; recommended depth is held at 2–3 in to protect roots.
evidence: A standard bag holds 2 cu ft of mulch.
2–3 in is the horticultural sweet spot — deeper can suffocate roots and rot stems.
The buffer covers settling and uneven coverage.

edging.title: Edging Calculator
edging.intro: How many edging pieces to border a bed.
edging.emptyBody: Pick a rectangle or circle and enter its size to see how much edging you need.
edging.how: Perimeter is the distance around the bed. Divide by the length of each edging section, round up, and add a buffer for corner cuts and overlap.
evidence: Rigid and coiled edging commonly comes in ~8 ft sections.
The buffer covers corner cuts and overlap.

bedArea.title: Bed Area Calculator
bedArea.intro: Measure a bed's area and perimeter — the starting point for every material estimate.
bedArea.emptyBody: Fill in the shape to see area and perimeter.
bedArea.formula: rectangle = L × W   ·   circle = π × r²
bedArea.how: Enter a shape and its dimensions; we report the area in both sq ft and sq m, plus the perimeter where the shape has one.
evidence: 1 sq m = 10.764 sq ft.
Drop this area into any of the material calculators.

material.title: Material Calculator
material.intro: How much topsoil, compost, gravel, sand, or bark to cover an area — by bag, cubic yard, or estimated tons.
material.emptyBody: Pick a material and fill in the area and depth.
material.formula: bags = ⌈ area × depth ÷ bag volume ⌉ + buffer   ·   cu yd = volume ÷ 27
material.how: Area × depth gives the loose volume to fill. We round up to whole bags and add a buffer for settling and waste; bulk delivery is shown in cubic yards (and an estimated weight for stone).
evidence: Bagged material is ~1–2 cu ft; the default bag size changes per material.
1 cubic yard = 27 cubic feet.
Stone weighs roughly 1.4 tons per cubic yard — it varies by stone, so it is shown as a range.

spacing.title: Plant Spacing Calculator
spacing.intro: How many plants fill a bed at a given spacing — square or triangular layout.
spacing.emptyBody: Fill in the bed size and how far apart the plants go.
spacing.formula: square: plants = area ÷ spacing²   ·   triangular: ~15% more
spacing.how: Each plant needs a spacing × spacing square of room. Triangular (offset) rows pack about 15% more plants into the same area. Counts round down so you never over-buy.
evidence: Spacing is center-to-center — from the plant tag or our plant library.
Triangular layout uses ~0.866× the area per plant.
Counts round down to whole plants.

watering.title: Watering Run-Time Calculator
watering.intro: How long to run a sprinkler to apply a target amount of water.
watering.emptyBody: Enter how fast your sprinkler applies water (inches per hour).
watering.how: Find your sprinkler's output rate with a catch-cup test — place cups, run 15 min, measure the average depth. Divide your target by that rate to get the run time.
evidence: Lawns usually want about 1 inch of water per session.
Output rate comes from a catch-cup test or the sprinkler's spec sheet.
On slopes or clay, split into shorter cycles to avoid runoff.

plantFinder.title: Plant Finder
plantFinder.intro: Find plants from the Bloomprint Core Library that actually fit your yard — by zone, sun, water, and safety.
plantFinder.noMatches: No catalog plants match those conditions yet — loosen a filter.
plantFinder.formula: match = zone ∧ sun ∧ water ∧ type ∧ safety, ranked by upkeep + resilience
plantFinder.how: We filter the curated Core Library to plants that satisfy every condition you set, then rank by ease of care and resilience. Hard filters (zone, safety) exclude — nothing is invented.
evidence: From the Bloomprint Core Library — curated and tuned for hardiness ~3–8 (not exhaustive).
Toxicity and invasive flags are conservative; confirm for your area.
Check the plant tag at the nursery before buying.

hardiness.title: Hardiness Zone Finder
hardiness.intro: Look up your USDA plant hardiness zone by ZIP — the number every plant tag (and our Plant Finder) uses.
hardiness.errNotFound: No zone found for that ZIP — check the digits, or use the USDA map.
hardiness.errUnreachable: Couldn't reach the zone service. Try again, or enter your zone manually.
hardiness.verify: Live from the USDA map — confirm before relying on it for borderline plants.
hardiness.usePlantFinder: Use this zone in the Plant Finder to see what thrives.
hardiness.how: We look up your ZIP against the USDA 2023 Plant Hardiness Zone Map (via phzmapi.org). Your zone is the band of average coldest winter temperatures; plants are rated for the coldest zone they survive.
evidence: Source: USDA 2023 Plant Hardiness Zone Map, via phzmapi.org (keyless).
Zones are 10°F bands; the 'a'/'b' suffix splits each in half.
Microclimates vary — a sheltered city yard can run a half-zone warmer.
hardiness.emptyBody: We'll look up your USDA hardiness zone.

soilPh.title: Soil pH Amendment
soilPh.intro: How much lime to raise — or sulfur to lower — your soil pH to a target, scaled by soil texture.
soilPh.noneBody: No lime or sulfur needed — re-test in a year.
soilPh.shiftWarnBody: Move pH no more than ~1.5 units per season. Apply in stages and re-test before adding more.
soilPh.assumeRate: Rates: extension-service figures per 1,000 sq ft per 1.0 pH unit, by texture.
soilPh.assumeRetest: A soil test is the real answer — this is a planning estimate.
soilPh.how: Limestone raises pH; elemental sulfur lowers it. Clay resists change (more product) and sand changes fast (less). We scale a per-1,000-sq-ft rate by your pH change, texture, and area.
evidence: Lime to raise 1.0 unit / 1,000 sq ft ≈ 25 lb (sand) · 40 (loam) · 50 (clay).
Sulfur to lower 1.0 unit / 1,000 sq ft ≈ 10 · 15 · 20 lb.
Soils buffer differently — confirm with a soil test before large changes.
soilPh.emptyBody: Add the area and your current and target pH.

fertilizer.title: Fertilizer (NPK) Calculator
fertilizer.intro: How much of a fertilizer to apply to hit a target nitrogen rate — and when to split it.
fertilizer.how: The bag's first number is its nitrogen percent. We work out the pounds of actual N your area needs, then divide by that percent to get product weight. Rates above 1 lb N are split into multiple feeds.
evidence: 1 lb N per 1,000 sq ft is a common single-feed turf rate.
Never apply more than ~1 lb soluble N at once — split higher rates.
Water in after applying; follow the product label.
fertilizer.emptyBody: Add the area, target nitrogen, and the bag's N%.

raisedBed.title: Raised-Bed Soil Blend
raisedBed.intro: Total fill for a raised bed, split into a topsoil / compost / aeration recipe — bags and cubic yards per part.
raisedBed.pctWarn: Percentages add to {sum}% — adjust them to total 100%.
raisedBed.formula: total = L × W × depth   ·   part = total × part%
raisedBed.how: We compute the bed's fill volume, then split it by your recipe. A 60/30/10 topsoil-compost-aeration mix is a solid default for most vegetables.
evidence: Default recipe: 60% topsoil, 30% compost, 10% aeration (perlite or fine bark).
1 cubic yard = 27 cubic feet; bagged mix is ~1.5 cu ft.
Beds settle — top up with compost each season.
raisedBed.emptyBody: Add length, width, and fill depth.

gardenAi.title: Garden AI Helper
gardenAi.intro: Ask a gardening question and get concise, honest guidance — powered by DeepSeek, with a built-in offline fallback.
gardenAi.placeholder: e.g. When should I prune hydrangeas?
gardenAi.error: Couldn't answer right now — try again.
prompts: Why are my tomato leaves turning yellow?
How often should I water newly planted shrubs?
gardenAi.formula: your question → DeepSeek (or offline guidance) → answer + tips
gardenAi.how: A single gardening question, answered concisely. When a DeepSeek key is configured it writes the reply; otherwise you get built-in guidance. Either way it sticks to general horticulture and won't invent prices, quantities, or plant-safety claims.
evidence: Powered by DeepSeek when configured; deterministic offline guidance otherwise.
General guidance only — confirm specifics on the plant tag or with a local extension office.
No prices, exact quantities, brand names, or safety claims are invented.
gardenAi.emptyBody: Pick a topic and type your question.

retainingWall.title: Retaining Wall Estimator
retainingWall.intro: Block courses, count, cap row, and the base + drainage gravel a wall actually needs.
retainingWall.recommend: Buy ~8% extra for cuts and breakage.
retainingWall.gravelNote: Base pad ≈ 12 in × 6 in trench; drainage ≈ 12 in of gravel behind the wall.
retainingWall.how: We work out how many courses tall and how many blocks long the wall is, add a waste margin and a cap row, then size the leveling-pad and behind-wall drainage gravel a sound wall needs.
evidence: A drainage layer + base pad is what keeps a wall from heaving — not optional.
Default block: 12 in face × 6 in tall (typical segmental block); change it to match yours.
Walls over ~3–4 ft usually need engineering and a permit — check locally.
retainingWall.emptyBody: Add the wall length and height.

fence.title: Fence Estimator
fence.intro: Posts, sections, rails, panels or pickets, and concrete from a run length and spacing.
fence.how: We divide the run by your post spacing for sections, add an end post and one per gate, then count rails, panels or pickets, and ~2 bags of concrete per post.
evidence: 8 ft is the common max post spacing for wood fences (6 ft for heavier panels).
Each post ≈ 2 bags of fast-setting concrete; gates need a sturdier post.
Call before you dig — locate utilities first.
fence.emptyBody: Add the total length to run.

frenchDrain.title: French Drain Estimator
frenchDrain.intro: Gravel, perforated pipe, filter fabric, and the minimum slope a trench needs to drain.
frenchDrain.how: We take the trench cross-section minus the pipe for gravel volume, wrap fabric around the trench, add pipe with a fitting margin, and compute the minimum end-to-end drop (≈1%) the drain needs to flow.
evidence: A drain needs ~1% slope (≈1 in per 8 ft) — flat trenches don't drain.
Wrap gravel in filter fabric so soil doesn't clog it; pipe holes face down.
Gravel ≈ 1.4 tons per cubic yard (varies by stone).
frenchDrain.emptyBody: Add the trench length; defaults cover width, depth, and pipe.
